    Compute study level effect sizes

    Source: R/meta-effect-size.R
    meta_effect_size.Rd

    meta_effect_size() adds an effect size (.yi), its sampling variance (.vi) and standard error (.sei) to every row of a data frame and returns a <meta_es> tibble that the rest of the package understands.

    Usage

    meta_effect_size(
  .data,
  measure = "SMD",
  ...,
  m1 = NULL,
  sd1 = NULL,
  n1 = NULL,
  m2 = NULL,
  sd2 = NULL,
  n2 = NULL,
  event1 = NULL,
  event2 = NULL,
  time1 = NULL,
  time2 = NULL,
  r = NULL,
  n = NULL,
  event = NULL,
  yi = NULL,
  vi = NULL,
  sei = NULL,
  study = NULL,
  add = 0.5,
  to = c("only0", "all", "none")
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame or tibble with one row per study (or per effect size).

    measure

    The effect size metric. See the Measures section.

    ...

    These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

    m1, sd1, n1, m2, sd2, n2

    <data-masking> Means, standard deviations and sample sizes of groups 1 and 2. n1 and n2 are also the group sizes for "RR" and "OR".

    event1, event2

    <data-masking> Number of events in groups 1 and 2.

    time1, time2

    <data-masking> Person time at risk in groups 1 and 2.

    r, n

    <data-masking> Correlation coefficients and sample sizes (n is also the total for "PLO").

    event

    <data-masking> Number of events for "PLO".

    yi, vi, sei

    <data-masking> Precomputed effect sizes with their variances or standard errors for "GEN".

    study

    <tidy-select> Optional column holding study labels, used in plots and tables.

    add

    Value added to cells for zero cell corrections.

    to

    Which studies receive the correction: "only0", "all" or "none".

    Value

    A <meta_es> tibble: .data plus the columns .yi, .vi and .sei.

    Measures

    "SMD"

    Standardised mean difference with Hedges' exact small sample correction (Hedges' g). Needs m1, sd1, n1, m2, sd2, n2. The variance is \(1/n_1 + 1/n_2 + g^2 / (2(n_1 + n_2))\).

    "MD"

    Raw mean difference, with variance \(sd_1^2/n_1 + sd_2^2/n_2\). Needs the same columns as "SMD".

    "RR"

    Log risk ratio. Needs event1, n1, event2, n2.

    "OR"

    Log odds ratio. Needs event1, n1, event2, n2.

    "IRR"

    Log incidence rate ratio. Needs event1, time1, event2, time2 (person time).

    "ZCOR"

    Fisher's z transformed correlation, with variance \(1/(n - 3)\). Needs r and n.

    "PLO"

    Logit transformed proportion. Needs event and n.

    "GEN"

    Generic, precomputed effect sizes. Needs yi and either vi or sei.

    Group 1 is the treatment or exposed group and group 2 the comparison group, so positive values favour group 1 having the larger mean, risk, odds or rate. The aliases "g", "logRR", "logOR", "logIRR", "fisher_z" and "logit" are also accepted.

    For the count based measures ("RR", "OR", "IRR", "PLO") the value of add is added to the cells of studies with a zero cell when to = "only0" (the default), to every study when to = "all", or never when to = "none".

    References

    Hedges, L. V. (1981). Distribution theory for Glass's estimator of effect size and related estimators. Journal of Educational Statistics, 6(2), 107-128. doi:10.3102/10769986006002107

    Borenstein, M., Hedges, L. V., Higgins, J. P. T. and Rothstein, H. R. (2009). Introduction to Meta-Analysis. Wiley.

    Examples

    # Log risk ratios for the BCG vaccine trials
bcg <- meta_effect_size(bcg_trials, "RR",
  event1 = tpos, n1 = tpos + tneg,
  event2 = cpos, n2 = cpos + cneg,
  study = author
)
bcg

# Hedges' g for length of hospital stay
meta_effect_size(stroke_los, "SMD",
  m1 = m1, sd1 = sd1, n1 = n1, m2 = m2, sd2 = sd2, n2 = n2
)
